classifications.rationale: The President directs federal departments, agencies, and instrumentalities concerning an internal procurement-reporting trigger; this fragment itself creates no substantive legal consequence for outside parties.
classifications.evidence: a department, agency or instrumentality of the Government shall hereafter receive two or more bids

classifications.rationale: After an agency determines that bids are identical, it must submit an internal report to the Attorney General within 20 days of the award; the consequence is administrative reporting, not a change in legal rights.
classifications.evidence: shall make a report of the bid proceedings to the Attorney General not later than 20 days following the award

classifications.rationale: The segment directs agencies to submit procurement reports, specifies their administrative contents and exceptions, and begins a parallel reporting trigger for property sales; none imposes a substantive legal outcome on bidders.
classifications.evidence: it shall make a report of such proceedings to the Attorney General not later than 20 days following the rejection

classifications.rationale: An agency that determines sale bids are identical must later report the proceedings to the Attorney General; this is internal executive information management.
classifications.evidence: shall make a report of the bid proceedings to the Attorney General not later than 20 days following the award to the purchaser

classifications.rationale: The segment establishes agency reporting duties and gives the Attorney General discretion to vary the order’s internal reporting requirements, without dictating a substantive legal result affecting outside parties.
classifications.evidence: The Attorney General is granted authority to establish reasonable exemptions and variations from the requirements of section 1 or of section 3

classifications.rationale: The Attorney General and other agency heads must consult, arrange historical reports, and establish procedures inviting state and local submissions; these are executive coordination and information-gathering measures.
classifications.evidence: The Attorney General shall formulate and put into effect procedures whereby State and local governments are invited to transmit reports to him

classifications.rationale: The Attorney General must periodically consolidate information, distribute the report, protect specified national-security information, and exercise delegated discretion consistently with the order’s enforcement purpose; these are reporting and internal-management directions.
classifications.evidence: the Attorney General shall make a report to the President consolidating the information he has received pursuant to this order

classifications.rationale: Federal agency heads must assist the Attorney General with analysis of reported data, an internal interagency cooperation duty.
classifications.evidence: shall cooperate with and aid the Attorney General in analyzing the data reported to him

classifications.rationale: Agency heads must make facilities available where possible and are encouraged to provide further collusion information; both actions concern internal investigative support rather than a dictated legal outcome.
classifications.evidence: shall make available to him to the fullest extent possible any facilities they may have which would expedite that work
